headline: Softer markets cut revenue, cost discipline narrows loss
summary_short: Coinbase's Q2 2026 total revenue fell to $1.22B (-18.5% y/y, -13.6% q/q) as softer crypto trading volumes weighed on transaction revenue, while the net loss narrowed q/q to $359M (diluted EPS -$1.36) from $394M as management held expenses below the midpoint of its Q2 outlook.
summary_long: Total revenue fell to $1.22B as a 25% q/q drop in crypto spot trading volume cut transaction revenue 21% q/q to $599M; subscription & services revenue held up better at $555M (48% of net revenue) on record USDC balances. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $208M as Adjusted Expenses of $1.03B came in below the outlook midpoint after a 14% May headcount cut. Net loss narrowed q/q to $359M (diluted EPS -$1.36) but reversed a $1.43B profit a year earlier, driven mainly by losses on crypto held for investment. Cash fell to $8.6B after $1.24B of buybacks and a $1.27B debt repayment. For Q3'26, Coinbase guides S&S revenue of $500-580M and cut full-year 2026 Adjusted Expenses guidance to $4.20-4.45B.

drivers.explanation: Management framed the quarter as strong fundamentals against macro headwinds: softening spot market conditions, an 11% q/q decline in total crypto market cap, and multi-year-low crypto asset volatility suppressed trading activity.
Transaction revenue declined 21% q/q, outperforming the 25% q/q decline in Total Market Crypto Spot Trading Volume; subscription & services revenue (48% of net revenue) partly offset the drop.

Consumer transaction revenue fell 20% q/q on a 24% q/q decline in consumer crypto spot volume, partially offset by growth in prediction markets; institutional revenue fell 26% q/q roughly in line with market declines.
Stablecoin revenue declined as new highs in average USDC held were offset by lower interest rates and off-platform balances; blockchain rewards fell on price effects and lower reward rates.
Lower revenue drove the decline even as Technology & Development, G&A, and Sales & Marketing expenses all fell q/q on proactive cost reductions announced in May, including a 14% headcount cut.

The y/y swing to a loss was driven mainly by a $209.5M loss on crypto assets held for investment this quarter versus a $362.1M gain a year earlier, plus a $52.4M restructuring charge; the operating loss also widened on lower revenue.
Debt fell after a $1.27B repayment of long-term debt during the first half of 2026.
